charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income

sections.title: Revenue Mix & Pipeline Products
sections.subtitle: Legacy MS products are declining as biosimilar competition and Tecfidera generics bite; Skyclarys, Qalsody, Zurzuvae and the Alzheimer's/Ocrevus royalty streams are the offset

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

revenueCategory.title: Revenue by category
revenueCategory.content:
Biogen's income statement splits revenue into product revenue (drugs it sells directly), anti-CD20 royalty revenue (its share of Roche/Genentech's Ocrevus and related anti-CD20 antibody sales), contract manufacturing, royalty & other revenue, and, from FY2024, Alzheimer's collaboration revenue (the Eisai-partnered Leqembi P&L split). These four lines sum exactly to total revenue.

For Biogen: the royalty and collaboration lines now carry more of the growth than product sales -- Ocrevus royalties and Leqembi are offsetting a shrinking branded-MS franchise.

What to watch:

  • Product revenue's declining share of the total
  • Alzheimer's collaboration revenue scaling as Leqembi volumes ramp (and whether Biogen's collaboration loss-sharing narrows)
  • Anti-CD20 royalty revenue is Roche's Ocrevus (and Rituxan/Gazyva) performance, not something Biogen controls directly

productMix.title: Product revenue by franchise
productMix.content:
The drug-level breakdown of product revenue: legacy multiple-sclerosis therapies (Tecfidera, Tysabri), the SMA drug Spinraza, the newer MS oral Vumerity, the biosimilars portfolio (Benepali/Flixabi/Imraldi), and the recent rare-disease launches Skyclarys (Friedreich's ataxia), Qalsody (SOD1-ALS) and Zurzuvae (postpartum depression).

For Biogen: this is the central investment question -- Tecfidera lost US exclusivity and generics have cut it by more than two-thirds since FY2021, and Tysabri faces biosimilar entry; Skyclarys, Qalsody and Zurzuvae are the bet that new launches outgrow that erosion before it overwhelms the base.

What to watch:

  • Combined growth-product revenue (Skyclarys + Qalsody + Zurzuvae) versus the combined decline in Tecfidera + Tysabri + Spinraza
  • Vumerity cannibalizing Tecfidera within the same MS franchise rather than adding net revenue
  • Biosimilars margin is much lower than branded product margin, so flat biosimilar revenue is not flat biosimilar profit

rd.title: R&D expense
rd.content:
R&D expense is spend on clinical trials, discovery and regulatory work; shown here against revenue as R&D intensity.

For Biogen: R&D fell sharply after the 2024 pipeline reprioritization (cutting several early-stage neurology programs), which is why the ratio has stepped down rather than drifted -- a one-off reset, not a trend to extrapolate.

What to watch:

  • Whether R&D re-accelerates to replace the MS/SMA franchises now in decline
  • R&D intensity versus large-cap pharma peers (typically 15-20% of revenue)

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Biogen Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Biogen Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Biogen Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Biogen Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Biogen Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Biogen Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Biogen Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Biogen Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Biogen Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Biogen Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
